args.title: checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after deploying v2.3.1 to production (all regions: us-east, us-west, eu-west). Error rate reached 18% and service status was unhealthy. Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production, in all regions. Rollback completed successfully; monitoring continues.

trace.final:
All done. Here's a summary of what I did:

## Summary

**Problem:** checkout-api was failing health checks after the latest deploy (v2.3.1) in all production regions, with an 18% error rate.

**Actions taken:**
1. **Investigated** — Confirmed v2.3.1 was unhealthy in production (all regions: us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. Deployment history showed v2.2.9 and v2.3.0 were the last healthy production releases; v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy (staging).
2. **Rolled back** — Rolled checkout-api back to **v2.3.0** (the most recent release that was healthy in production) in all regions. Rollback completed successfully.
3. **Opened incident** — Created SEV2 incident **INC-0001** ("checkout-api unhealthy after v2.3.1 deploy - rolled back to v2.3.0"), which paged the on-call engineer, documenting the failure and the rollback.

**Verification:** Post-rollback status confirms checkout-api is now on v2.3.0 in all regions, **healthy**, with error rate back down to 0.2%.

Note: v2.3.1 was never healthy in production, so if it's redeployed later, that would require change-manager approval per policy.
